newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Only modest gains seen for South Australia - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Only modest gains seen for South Australia - REPORT.

text.p: South Australia's economy will experience modest gains at best for the rest of 1997, according to the SA Centre for Economic Studies which said the state remains a prisoner of its low growth in income, employment and population.

The centre's March 1997 briefing said while adjusted employment growth in Australia over the year to January had been a very buoyant 2.9 percent on an annualised basis, SA's employment had shown about zero growth.
The centre cautioned the recent growth in building and housing sales figures in SA may have been oversold and it forecast continuation of a somewhat weak market.

"While there does seem to be some increased activity in the upper end of the market (A$200,000), perhaps extending down to the middle, this would appear to be driven more by the availability of bargains," it said.
"There is not likely to be a significant lift in activity until we see sustained growth in income, employment and population," it said.
The report said economic growth in SA had slowed to two percent in real terms in the year to September 1996, just over half the national rate, while spending grew at 2.2 percent.

Poor profitability had caused SA's growth rate to fall below that of other states, and an increase in private equipment expenditure in the September quarter had contributed most to the growth the state had had, it said.

"Private new capital expenditure is now growing more strongly in South Australia than in any other state but its pronounced cyclical behaviour suggests caution as to whether the improvement can be sustained over the longer-term," it said.
Recent retail sales and new motor vehicle registrations suggested spending in the SA economy remained relatively flat, it said.

In the rural sector, the report said favourable seasonal conditions over the last two years had produced exceptional wheat and barley harvests and export growth of wine is expected to continue at record levels over the medium term.

It said the State government was on track to achieve a balanced (non-commercial) budget by 1997/98 after a vigorous programme of asset disposal and fiscal restraint but warned of any loosening of the purse strings with an election on the way.

The centre warned of the impact of a reduction in tariffs affecting the automotive industry from 25 to five percent, with its modelling predicting this would hit SA gross state product by 0.2 percent, around A$60 million and cost about 2,400 jobs.
